title: From planning to action: Fundamental insights on movement planning in the brain
description: When the signal sounds, all the runners push off from their starting blocks and set off sprinting. We can act within fractions of a second because we plan movements in our brains in advance, before carrying them out. At the interdisciplinary research center BrainLinks–BrainTools at the University of Freiburg, a team of 15 researchers from the fields of biology, artificial intelligence and neurotechnology has investigated in greater detail how the transition from mentally preparing a movement to actually executing it with one's muscles is controlled at the neural level. In their article, published in the journal Cell Reports, the researchers propose an improved model for understanding the neural processes involved in movement planning.
